questions.why: Quatre-vingts takes an -s when it ends the number. Add anything after it and the -s disappears: quatre-vingt-cinq.
From 70 French counts by arithmetic: soixante-dix is sixty-ten, and 71 is sixty-and-eleven. The 1990 reform allows the hyphenated spelling too.

questions.q: Which of these does NOT take « et » ?
questions.why: 21, 31, 41, 51, 61 and 71 use et with no hyphen. 81 and 91 break the pattern: quatre-vingt-un, quatre-vingt-onze.
Literally four-twenty-seventeen. No -s on quatre-vingt here, because something follows it.

questions.q: Type the number you hear, in digits.
questions.why: The tens up to soixante are regular, and 42 is simply quarante plus deux with a hyphen.
Cent takes -s only when it is the last element: deux cents euros. As soon as another number follows, the -s vanishes.
Mille is invariable and never takes an -s, unlike cent and vingt. Des milliers exists but means thousands, an approximation, not 2 000.

questions.q: Complete: « un million ___ habitants » (a million inhabitants)
questions.why: Million and milliard are nouns, not numbers: they take un in front and de before the noun that follows, elided here to d'.

questions.q: Type the number you hear, in digits.
questions.why: Sixty-fifteen. Anything in the seventies is soixante plus a number from ten to nineteen.

questions.q: On a French price tag you see « 3,14 ». What is it?
choices: three thousand one hundred and forty
questions.why: France uses a comma as the decimal point and a space or dot for thousands. So 19,99 € is nineteen euros ninety-nine, and 1 000 000 is a million.

questions.q: How does the x of « six » sound in « six ans » ?
choices: like a z, linking onto ans
questions.why: Before a vowel the x links as a z. Before a consonant it goes silent (six livres), and standing alone it is a hard s (il y en a six).

questions.why: Four-twenty-thirteen. The nineties are quatre-vingt plus a teen, so you have to hold two additions at once.
Ordinals add -ième, but neuf changes its f to v first. Compare quatre, which drops its -e (quatrième), and cinq, which inserts a u (cinquième).
97 spoken as one word group, four-twenty-seventeen. Getting it out at speed is the only way the arithmetic stops slowing you down.

questions.q: When does « cent » take an -s, and when does it not? Give an example of each.
a: Cent takes -s when it is multiplied and ends the number: deux cents euros. It loses the -s as soon as another number follows: deux cent dix euros. Plain cent (100) never takes one. Quatre-vingts follows the same rule; mille never takes an -s at all.
questions.why: The rule is about position, not size: an -s only survives at the end of the number. That single test covers cent and vingt together.
